Kozlov’s Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 6.7 show that each circular connected-factor component collapses onto a positive n-step sink core, so α evaluates n on a primitive H1 generator; the integral normalization is unique. A graph isomorphism preserves sinks, hence α and this generator. Kozlov Definition 2.9(3) makes disconnected F(G) the exact product; all factor homology is free, so Künneth gives exterior powers and Eilenberg–Zilber swaps give only the Koszul sign. For invariant b, tr(∧^q P)=[t^q]det(I+tP)=the product of 1−(−t)^d over cycles. Rational finite-group quotient homology is the invariant subspace after equivariant triangulation, proving the average. Boundary q=0, q>|I_b| and empty component cases match. Independent direct orientation checks: 43 connected labeled graphs on n=2..4, 564 state-level cocycle-square tests, 14048 automorphism/state/vertex sign checks; independent 2-circle factor swap yields H0/H1/H2 traces 1/0/−1 and quotient rational b=(1,1,0). These finite checks are corroboration; the general proof relies on the verified published core theorem and standard Künneth/transfer.
